newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MHS hopeful of Air Cambodge investment.
newsitem.headline: MHS hopeful of Air Cambodge investment.

text.p: Malaysian Helicopter Services Bhd (MHS) said on Wednesday it was hopeful that Royal Air Cambodge Ltd could be made profitable as Cambodia becomes a member of ASEAN and its political climate improves.

"Royal Air Cambodge has not started to make money," MHS executive chairman Saw Huat Lye told reporters after the company's annual meeting. "Certainly for Royal Air Cambodge we hope to be able to turn that around in a couple of years."
The airline was formed in December 1994, with MHS holding a 40 percent equity interest and the Cambodian government the remaining 60 percent.
Saw said tourists are shying away from Cambodia due to its political problems. Tensions are high in the country following recent fighting between security officials loyal to the two prime ministers.
Cambodia's entry into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) at the end of July and its attractive tourist sites would help the airline, he said.
"Royal Air Cambodge must sooner or later make a lot of money," Saw said.
Saw said MHS was less bullish about its investment in Air Maldives Ltd due to the small tourist flow into the Indian Ocean island nation. MHS holds a 49 percent interest in the airline.
"Most come from Europe. They are basically winter traffic for sand, sun and sea," Saw said.
He said MHS's profits would continue to be heavily dependent on Malaysian Airline System Bhd, in which MHS has a 29.1 percent stake.
"The bulk of it (profits), yes, it would come from MAS for the next year at least," he said.
